rubric.label: Operations fit
rubric.explanation: Analyst-scored from 22 to 30 for evidence that a traceability, inspection, or work-instruction workflow fits the public MASS Group product scope. A specific production or shop handoff earns the highest values.

rubric.label: Signal specificity
rubric.explanation: Analyst-scored from 20 to 30. Segment growth disclosures score 20, dated expansion research or integration milestones score 24–28, and a named site opening or production transfer scores 30.

rubric.label: DoD award recency
rubric.explanation: 25 points for an award start in the previous 365 days, 21 for 366–730 days, and 17 for older records visible in the query window.

rubric.label: Stakeholder evidence
rubric.explanation: 15 points for two or more company-confirmed named roles, 12 for one confirmed and one sourced candidate, and 10 for one confirmed role.

accounts.name: StandardAero
accounts.fit: StandardAero operates engine MRO shops for commercial and government customers. A shop-level repair traveler is a practical TME® use case because receiving, routing, inspections, and release records must stay tied to one serialized job.

signal.title: Winnipeg MRO expansion opened
signal.fact: StandardAero reported that its Winnipeg expansion increased the facility footprint by 40% and expanded engine MRO capacity.

accounts.awardContext: The U.S. award names Standard Aero (San Antonio) Inc. for public depot maintenance work. The Winnipeg news is a separate corporate MRO capacity signal.
accounts.hypothesis: A growing shop network may benefit from a common traveler and inspection format that preserves local work instructions.
accounts.validation: Ask which U.S. or Canadian shop owns traveler templates, where inspection evidence is stored, and whether a shop is standardizing its workflow. Confirm the incumbent MRO and ERP systems.
